name: Shelemiah
overview: Shelemiah is a male figure noted in Scripture as a descendant of Bani. He is distinguished by the unique attribute of having married a foreign wife, a detail recorded in Ezra 10:41. The biblical text does not specify his tribal affiliation or additional personal notes.
namesAndTitles: The name Shelemiah means 'YHWH pays back' or possibly 'He restores peace offering of YHWH,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in the Hebrew language. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God in the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Shelemiah as a descendant of Bani, establishing a clear familial link. Beyond this, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shelemiah's significance in the biblical narrative centers on his identity as a descendant of Bani who married a foreign wife, highlighting the post-exilic community's challenges in maintaining covenant purity. His mention in Ezra 10:41 situates him within the broader context of the restoration period when the people of Israel were called to separate from foreign influences. This underscores the ongoing call for faithfulness to God's covenant in the face of social and cultural pressures.
